title: NimbleHealth savings delta workup (before / after Redwood Optimize)
content:
Purpose

Quick customer-specific before/after cost model and prioritized recommendations for NimbleHealth. This is a working spreadsheet-style export with assumptions, line-item cost deltas, and implementation notes for the Redwood Optimize playbook applied to NimbleHealth’s production workload. Aim is to surface an expected monthly savings range and implementation effort estimate for sales/CS and engineering planning.

Executive summary (high level)

- Baseline monthly inference spend (hosted + dedicated bursts): ~$45,200/mo (current mix of third-party hosted + customer edge GPUs)
- Redwood Optimize recommended stack yields projected spend: $17,900/mo -> ~60% cost reduction on inference line (recurring)
- Key levers: prefix/KV caching (cached prefixes + session affinity), workload-aware batching, move to smaller quantized model variants for assistant responses, and request routing to dedicated reserved capacity for high-throughput routes.
- Estimated implementation timeline: 4–8 weeks (staged: caching + routing 2–3 weeks; model switch + quantization 2–4 weeks; ops + monitoring 1–2 weeks).

Baseline workload & assumptions

- Customer: NimbleHealth (telehealth/clinical triage chat + embeddings for retrieval)
- Monthly active sessions: 80k
- Avg requests per session: 7 (mix of short prompts and multi-turn clarifications)
- Monthly tokens (input + output): 1.85B tokens (1.05B input, 0.8B output)
- P95 latency requirement (chat flows): <= 350ms
- Concurrency observed: peaks ~120 concurrent generation streams; typical sustained 45–60
- Current model mix: 60% rw-7b-prod (float16), 30% rw-3.5-gen (float16), 10% embedding-large (float16)
- Current average cost per 1M tokens (weighted): $24.5 (effective across hosted and dedicated bursts)
- Current unit economics: monthly inference-only cost ~45,200; ops overhead (monitoring/transfer/infra) additional but out-of-scope for immediate model-level savings.

Redwood Optimize recommendations (summary)

1) Per-session KV/prefix caching (long-context reuse): recommended
   - Why: NimbleHealth has long recurring session prompts and high repetition (templates + intake forms) -> high cache hit potential
   - Expected impact: ~30% token reduction (less actual model compute) on chat flows; effective compute cost reduction for those sessions
   - Risk: correctness for personalization tokens; need expire/invalidations for clinical context
   - Implementation notes: store KV cache keyed by hashed session-template + recent messages; TTL 24h for non-sensitive contexts; integrate with private deployment KMS for PII handling.

2) Batching policy tuning and dynamic batching windows: recommended
   - Why: high sustained concurrency with many short inputs; batching yields lower per-token GPU cost while preserving p95 if windows tuned
   - Expected impact: ~12–18% cost savings (depends on peak smoothing)
   - Risk: increased tail latency if overly aggressive; mitigation by latency-aware routing and burst capacity fallback.

3) Model family rationalization + quantized variants: recommended
   - Path: move lower-critical responses (clarifications, non-medical helpers) to rw-3.5-q4/8 and keep rw-7b-q4 for clinical summation and safety-critical output
   - Expected impact: ~10–15% cost reduction by shifting mix + quantized int8 or q4_0 where quality tolerable
   - Quality guardrails: run A/B with eval prompts (see linked eval set) and monitor QA regression (automated eval suite).

4) Route high-volume, low-sensitivity embedding requests to batch-only pipelines (and time-shift indexing): recommended
   - Why: embeddings are heavy cost; batch offline if not needed real-time
   - Expected impact: up to 8% of total baseline cost (embedding line) eliminated from hot-path.

5) Reserved Dedicated capacity for 2 top routes + on-demand fallback: optional but high ROI for 24/7 chat flows
   - Why: predictable throughput and unit-cost reduction for committed utilization
   - Expected impact: further 6–10% on top of Optimizations if commit levels match sustained throughput.

Before / After high-level numbers (monthly) - working model

- Baseline (current): $45,200/mo
  - chat model compute: $31,400
  - embeddings: $7,800
  - buffer/burst hosted: $6,000

- After Redwood Optimize (conservative): $17,900/mo
  - chat model compute: $11,000 (post-caching, batching, quant)
  - embeddings (batched/off-peak): $3,200
  - reserved/dedicated amortized: $3,700 (cost of commit but lower per-token)
  - implementation amortized (first 3 months): not included in monthly run-rate above

Estimated delta and payback

- Absolute monthly savings: ~$27,300
- Percent savings: ~60% reduction vs baseline
- Estimated one-time implementation effort (eng FTE weeks): ~6–10 developer-weeks (distributed across infra, runtime, and product)
- Minimal expected payback (recoup infra effort) based purely on monthly savings: implementation cost payback in ~6–10 weeks when accounting for small integration/validation testing costs (detailed in project plan).

Line-item sensitivity scenarios (quick)

- Pessimistic: cache hit rate low (10%), batching limited (5% uplift) -> savings drop to ~28% (cost = ~$32,500/mo)
- Base case: cache hit 30%, batching 15%, model mix shift 10% -> savings ~60% (cost = ~$17,900/mo)
- Aggressive: cache hit 45%, batching 25%, reserved commit matches 80% sustained -> savings ~72% (cost = ~$12,700/mo)

Implementation plan (phased)

1) Measurement & telemetry (week 0–1): add instrumentation to measure prefix reuse ratio, request size distribution, token-level counts by route. (JIRA:PRODOPT-278)
2) KV/Prefix caching pilot (week 1–3): implement server-side cache for top 10 session templates; validate correctness and hit rates; smoke test with canary traffic (~5% users)
3) Batching policy rollout (week 2–4): incrementally tune batching windows per route; set latency SLO guards with fallback
4) Quantized model rollout (week 3–6): stage A/B with rw-3.5-q4/8 for non-critical flows; monitor eval metrics and safety regressions
5) Routing + reserved commit plan (week 4–8): negotiate commit for dedicated capacity for top two routes once steady-state savings validated

Open questions / unknowns

- Exact paydown of existing third-party hosted contracts if we switch heavy volume to reserved capacity (legal/commercial coordination needed).
- PII handling for cache keys: need privacy engineering sign-off on how we hash/salt keys and TTLs.
- Realistic cache hit baseline: current telemetry lacks fine-grained prefix-hash metrics (captured in measurement step).

Notes to self / for CS handoff

- Prepare two slide decks: 1) 1-pager ROI for customer exec; 2) technical runbook for implementation
- Ask Solutions Eng to run a 3-week canary with customer opt-in for caching pilot
- Update the linked spreadsheet with per-route token histograms (tab: route-token-hist) and an eval prompt set (tab: clinical-evals)

Attachments referenced (sheets/ids)

- Working model: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Nimble_Optimize_Model (contains tabbed scenarios: baseline, conservative, aggressive, sensitivity)
- Eval set: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPT/NimbleHealth+Baseline+Eval

Next steps (short)

- Align with CS on customer opt-in and timeline (this week)
- Spike telemetry changes and surface cache-hit metric (owner: Ethan Li)
- Book Solutions Eng pilot window and request SRE review for batching safety controls

-- end of working export --
